title: Beta rollout + metrics monitoring for SDK parity (auth/retry/timeout/streaming)
creator: Talia Benson
body:
Context
We are shipping standardized SDK behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go for auth precedence, retries/backoff, timeouts, and streaming semantics. This ticket covers the rollout mechanics: beta releases, internal dogfooding, monitoring dashboards, and explicit rollback triggers.

Rollout goals
- Validate that new defaults do not cause retry storms (esp. during elevated 429s) and do not materially degrade tail latency.
- Confirm the conformance suite is catching mismatches (no “works in TS but not in Python” regressions).
- Confirm request_id propagation + standardized logging fields are available for Support/Oncall triage.
- Verify streaming disconnect behavior is predictable behind proxies and that guidance is adequate.

Scope
- Beta release plan (versioning, packaging, docs positioning)
- Dogfooding plan (internal services + Redwood Console workflows)
- Monitoring plan (dashboards, metrics, alert thresholds, daily check-ins)
- Rollback triggers + decision owners

Non-goals
- Implement retry/timeout behavior changes themselves (tracked in language-specific tickets)
- Major gateway behavior changes beyond required consistency fields (tracked in ENG-5130)

Beta release strategy
1) Beta tags / prerelease channels
- TypeScript: publish as npm dist-tag `beta` (e.g., `@redwood-ai/sdk@x.y.z-beta.N`).
- Python: publish to PyPI as prerelease (e.g., `redwood-sdk==x.y.zbN`) and mirror to internal index used by dogfood services.
- Go: use module version suffix `-beta.N` and update internal consumers via go.mod overrides in dogfood repos.

2) “Beta behavior” policy
- Defaults are the new standardized defaults (retries/timeouts/auth precedence) unless explicitly blocked by language owner due to breaking change risk.
- Any compatibility toggles MUST be documented in migration notes and MUST be testable in conformance fixtures.

3) Canary cohorts
- Internal dogfood first (48–72 hours). If stable, move to 3–5 external canary customers (Support + PM to nominate; avoid heavily stateful flows for streaming retries).
- If any rollback trigger hits, pause expansion immediately and revert to last stable versions for canaries.

Internal dogfooding plan (owners)
- Redwood Console (web + backend) integration smoke tests: Dana Lo + Sahana Iyer
- DevEx sample apps / examples repo quickstart runs: Sabrina James
- CLI / internal tools that hit Hosted API: Ibrahim Khan
- Oncall “chaos” test window: Allison Grant + Sean Gallagher

What “good” looks like during dogfood
- No increase in 429 retry amplification (requests/sec after retries) beyond expected.
- Retry counts align with policy (no retries on 4xx except 408/409/429).
- Retry-After respected on 429 (including date format).
- Streaming: disconnect surfaces a typed error containing request_id when available; partial output is surfaced consistently.
- Timeouts: overall timeout is enforced for non-streaming; streaming has read timeout semantics consistent with ADR and does not hang indefinitely.

Monitoring + dashboards
Primary dashboards (must be live before beta expands beyond internal):
- SDK Retry/Timeout Overview (by language, version, endpoint):
  - retry_rate (attempts > 1 / total)
  - attempts_per_request p50/p95
  - backoff_time_total_ms p50/p95
  - timeout_rate (overall/connect/read where available)
  - request_id_missing_rate in errors
  - streaming_disconnect_rate + top reasons
- Gateway 429 + Retry-After health:
  - 429 rate by route + region
  - Retry-After present rate on 429
  - distribution of Retry-After seconds (sanity)

Proposed source of truth: “sdk-retry-timeout-dashboards-spec” (Drive) and Observability Pack PR adding panels.

Rollout check cadence
- Daily 15-min check-in during beta week 1 (DevEx + SRE + release coord)
- Post-check summary in #eng-sre + #devex: metrics snapshot, notable incidents, action items

Rollback triggers (hard)
Roll back beta / stop expansion if ANY of the following occurs:
1) Retry storm indicator
- attempts_per_request p95 increases by >0.30 vs baseline for >30 minutes AND 429 rate is elevated OR customer traffic is stable (suggests client-side amplification).
2) Elevated error rates attributable to SDK behavior
- 5xx + network error + timeout error rate increases by >25% vs baseline for >60 minutes in any one language during internal dogfood, or any increase observed in external canaries.
3) Streaming instability regressions
- streaming_disconnect_rate increases by >20% vs baseline for >60 minutes for canary cohort OR any reproducible case of stream hang without timeout/cancellation observed by dogfood.
4) Incorrect retry classification
- Verified retries on non-retryable 4xx (400/401/403/404/422) in beta builds, confirmed via logs or conformance failures.
5) request_id missing in raised errors
- request_id_missing_rate > 1% for SDK-thrown errors in beta builds (except for pure DNS/TCP failures where no server response exists).

Rollback decision owner
- Connor O’Brien (release) + Sean Gallagher (SRE) jointly decide. In case of disagreement, Sean makes the call for reliability.

Comms + docs
- PM-948 governs external comms; this ticket ensures the beta language is consistent:
  - “Beta channel available for standardized retries/timeouts; stable remains unchanged until GA.”
  - Include guidance on idempotency keys for safe retries (esp. for streaming).
  - Provide explicit config snippets for disabling retries or tightening timeouts.

Deliverables / acceptance criteria
- Beta versions published for all 3 SDKs with consistent release notes.
- Internal dogfood complete with documented results (metrics snapshot + issues found).
- Dashboards live with agreed thresholds; SRE confirms alert routing.
- Canary cohort defined and invited; opt-out path documented.
- Rollback runbook written (what to revert, who to page, customer message template).

Links
- Epic: ENG-5120 SDK parity audit
- Conformance suite: ENG-5127
- Telemetry/log fields: ENG-5129
- Platform gateway consistency: ENG-5130
- Observability dashboard panels: observability-pack PR-544
- SDK repo PRs (beta candidates):
  - Python: PR-857 conformance runner; PR-854 streaming errors; PR-850 timeout model; PR-846 retry policy
  - TS: PR-1302 timeouts; PR-1307 Retry-After; PR-1311 streaming
  - Go: PR-635 harness; PR-619 timeouts; PR-612 retries; PR-624 streaming types

Open questions
- Do we require a feature flag to keep old timeout defaults in stable for one release, or do we rely on clear migration notes? (Henry Cho + Monica Patel decision)
- For streaming, do we recommend automatic retry only when no tokens have been emitted? Current standard says conservative; confirm wording in docs (Wei Chen).
comments: 2026-01-29 (Connor O’Brien): Drafted beta plan. Waiting on confirmation from Nadia/Logan on which standardized logging fields are guaranteed across all SDKs in beta (retry_count, timeout_ms, streaming_disconnect_reason).

2026-02-03 (Allison Grant): SRE preference is to treat retry amplification as the primary rollback trigger. Please add explicit comparison window and baseline selection method (suggest: previous 7-day same-hour p95).

2026-02-05 (Ibrahim Khan): Noted from #incidents thread last quarter: retry storms correlated with 429 spikes + clients ignoring Retry-After. Ensure gateway Retry-After presence is monitored alongside SDK retry behavior, otherwise we’ll misattribute.

2026-02-08 (Sahana Iyer): Conformance suite now running in Python CI; Go harness integration is in review. For rollout, we should gate beta publish on conformance passing in all 3 languages for the tagged commits (manual checklist item).

2026-02-11 (Dana Lo): TS beta candidate should include PR-1316 (auth env var deprecation warnings) to avoid splitting the rollout message. I’ll provide recommended npm version + dist-tag timeline once merged.

2026-02-14 (Sean Gallagher): Added hard stop: if we see retries on any 4xx besides 408/409/429, treat as immediate rollback. Duplicate billing concerns are primarily perception, but we can’t afford broken classification. Also, confirm that retries are capped to max_attempts and that max_attempts is logged.

2026-02-18 (Wei Chen): Docs team requests one canonical snippet per language for “tight timeouts for streaming behind proxies” and “disable retries.” Please ensure beta notes link to the migration guide draft.

2026-02-21 (Connor O’Brien): Updated rollback trigger definitions per SRE feedback and added decision owner. Next: finalize canary customer list with Dev + Henry; schedule internal dogfood window for 2026-02-24 once Go/TS beta candidates are tagged.
